plain_meaning: Adjusted change in the modeled outcome per one-unit increase in the predictor, conditional on other terms in that model.
why_we_used_it: A β=0.33 means roughly +0.33 somatic-score points per 1 g/dL larger Hb deficit, conditional on G and X, if using that exact additive model.

plain_meaning: Range produced by the survey-design inference procedure that represents uncertainty around β.
why_we_used_it: If the interval excludes 0, the two-sided test usually gives p<0.05.
do_not_overclaim: A narrow CI is precision, not biological importance.

plain_meaning: Probability, under the fitted null model and survey design, of a test statistic at least this extreme if the tested coefficient were zero.
why_we_used_it: Used here for design-based Wald inference.
do_not_overclaim: Not the probability that the hypothesis is true.

plain_meaning: Descriptive fraction of weighted outcome variance accounted for by a fitted model.
do_not_overclaim: Not the primary NHANES inferential statistic.

plain_meaning: Increase in weighted R² after adding a term/block to a nested model.
why_we_used_it: Shows unique incremental descriptive information beyond existing terms.
do_not_overclaim: 0.0026 = 0.26 percentage points of weighted outcome variance, not 26%.

plain_meaning: Design-based test of whether an added term or block contributes after the rest of the model.
do_not_overclaim: Depends on survey design degrees of freedom.

plain_meaning: Effective inferential degrees of freedom driven mainly by PSU/stratum structure, not raw participant N.
why_we_used_it: 2021–23 has many participants but X3 exhausts residual design df.
do_not_overclaim: When residual df=0, t-based CI/p are not estimable.

plain_meaning: Comparative fit index for the latent-factor model; closer to 1 means better relative fit.
why_we_used_it: Used to compare one-factor versus two-factor PHQ structure.
do_not_overclaim: Good fit does not prove the factor model is uniquely true.

plain_meaning: Approximate model misfit per degree of freedom; smaller is better.
why_we_used_it: Used with CFI/SRMR rather than alone.

plain_meaning: Average standardized discrepancy between observed and model-implied relationships; smaller is better.
do_not_overclaim: Should be interpreted jointly with other fit measures.

plain_meaning: Standardized strength linking a PHQ item to a latent factor.
why_we_used_it: Sleep/fatigue/appetite load on the somatic factor.
do_not_overclaim: A loading does not mean an item is caused by physiology.

plain_meaning: Share of standardized marker variation captured by a principal component.
why_we_used_it: Used to ask whether one-number A/G proxies discard stable measurement structure.
do_not_overclaim: Principal components are mathematical axes, not automatically biological mechanisms.

plain_meaning: Similarity of component loading vectors after sign/order alignment across independently fit cycles.
why_we_used_it: Near 1 means the measurement pattern reproduced strongly.
do_not_overclaim: Stability does not by itself establish clinical meaning.

plain_meaning: Tests whether a specific PHQ item has a direct physiology association beyond the latent factor; FDR controls multiplicity.
why_we_used_it: No FDR-stable single-item effect was found.
do_not_overclaim: Useful negative check against one item driving the result.
